claims.text: The Pulumi docs page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ ('Output value errors') exists and covers symptoms of treating an Output as a plain value, including the placeholder text 'Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported'.

When an Output<T> is converted to a string in Pulumi (e.g. via toString), the resulting placeholder text reads 'Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported', which can appear in log lines, generated files, or resource properties.

The Troubleshooting index links to a page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ that diagnoses errors from stringifying, branching on, or reading a Pulumi output value like a plain value.
Pulumi produces the error "409 conflict: Another update is currently in progress" when concurrent updates occur.
X86_64 binaries running under Rosetta 2 on Apple Silicon can cause crashes or hangs.
Running `pulumi logs share` securely sends the logs from a failed operation to the Pulumi team.
A recently deleted stack can be recovered from the Pulumi Cloud console, including after an accidental `pulumi stack rm --force`.
`pulumi` supports `--target` and `--exclude` flags to limit operations to specific resources.
The CLI produces `read ".pulumi/meta.yaml"` errors when it can't access a self-managed state backend.

In TypeScript, converting a Pulumi Output to a string directly (e.g., in a template literal) does not throw by default and instead yields placeholder text such as `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, with guidance to use `apply` or `pulumi.interpolate`.
In TypeScript, calling `JSON.stringify()` on a Pulumi Output produces a `Calling [toJSON] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` string rather than the value.
In Python, converting a Pulumi Output to a string yields text such as `Calling __str__ on an Output[T] is not supported` and Pulumi logs a warning.
In Python, passing a Pulumi Output to `json.dumps()` fails with `TypeError: Object of type Output is not JSON serializable`; `Output.json_dumps()` is the alternative.
In Go, passing a `pulumi.StringOutput` where a `string` is expected is a compile error; values are resolved via `ApplyT`.
In C#, converting a Pulumi Output to a string yields text such as `Calling [ToString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, with guidance to use `Apply` or `Output.Format`.
Setting the environment variable `PULUMI_ERROR_OUTPUT_STRING=true` makes Output-to-string conversion throw an exception instead of returning placeholder text, in TypeScript, Python, and C#.

String-composition helpers: `pulumi.interpolate` and `pulumi.concat` in TypeScript; `Output.concat`/`Output.format`/`Output.json_dumps` in Python; `pulumi.Sprintf`/`pulumi.JSONMarshal` in Go; `Output.Format` in C#.
The `apply` callback runs asynchronously once the output resolves, generally after the program's top-level code has finished.
Most resource inputs accept Outputs as well as plain values; a resource's logical name cannot be an Output.
In dynamically typed languages an `if` on a Pulumi Output is generally always true, and in statically typed languages it is usually a compile error because Output<bool> is not bool.
Values known at program start, such as stack config read with `pulumi.Config`, environment variables, or hardcoded flags, are plain values that can be branched on normally.
Passing an Output as a resource logical name or loop bound fails to compile in TypeScript, Go, and C#.
In Python, passing an Output as a resource's logical name raises `TypeError: Expected resource name to be a string`.
In Python, `range(some_output)` raises `TypeError: 'Output' object cannot be interpreted as an integer`.
In Python, using an Output as a dictionary key does not raise; it silently keys on the Output object itself.

Pulumi has no supported way to block a program and synchronously read a resolved value from an Output; awaiting or reading synchronously fails to compile, fails at runtime, or returns placeholder text.
`pulumi stack output <name>` reads a single stack output after deployment.
The Automation API exposes an `outputs` field on the result of running an update (e.g., `res.Outputs` in Go).
Linked docs targets exist: /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/#outputs, /apply/, /all/, /docs/iac/concepts/stacks/#stackreferences, /docs/iac/concepts/automation-api/.
